dossier.public_summary: The signal is built from one or two very deep, highly variable dips that look different in different sectors and transits, and odd and even dips differ. This pattern matches a blended or systematic eclipsing binary folded at the wrong period, not a regular 4.2 Earth-radius planet on a 13.9-day orbit.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by 4.3 sigma with a factor of 2.3 in depth, consistent with an eclipsing binary folded at half its true period (period_x2 27.8 d) rather than a planet.

Depth is not steady even within the same QLP product, changing by more than an order of magnitude and essentially undetected in the 2-min data, as expected when the signal comes from a few deep bad events blended differently between sectors.
reasons.value: verdict changes_within_a_source, p_constant 4.46e-100, chi2 463.2 dof 3, depth_change_pct 215.6 (361 ppm in SPOC 2-min sector 19 vs 23568 ppm QLP sector 59, 12759 ppm sector 73, 6377 ppm sector 86)

reasons.why: One or two extremely deep transits dominate the folded signal (938% of signal from top 3), with other epochs showing no dip or opposite sign, so the folded depth and period are set by outliers, not a consistent planet transit.
reasons.value: 6 transits, share_of_top_3 0.938, p_consistent 6.609353026164633e-77, outliers 23101 ppm (sigma 12.0) and 24346 ppm (sigma 9.9) at BTJD 2925.3 and 2911.361, others ~795 ppm and -74 ppm

reasons.why: Marginal second dip near phase 0.33 comparable to the strongest systematics, not a clear planet occultation, but supports an alternative stellar-eclipse scenario over a planet.
